sentence: NHS stop smoking services offer nicotine replacement, medicines and professional support, and people in England can self-refer through NHS Better Health.
note: NHS stop smoking services: NRT, varenicline, bupropion, professional support; self-refer in England via Better Health

sentence: NHS stop smoking services provide nicotine replacement therapy and prescription medicines, together with professional support in the first months after quitting.
note: Services provide NRT and medicines, information and advice, professional support

sentence: Vapes are not available as medicines on the NHS, though some local services may offer a free starter pack.
note: E-cigarettes are not available as medicines; some local services may offer a free starter pack

sentence: The NHS says cravings are short-lived and that withdrawal symptoms are temporary.
note: NHS: cravings only last up to 15 minutes; withdrawal symptoms temporary

sentence: NHS Better Health also offers a personal quit plan and the NHS Quit Smoking app.
note: NHS offers free personalised 8-step quit plan and app

sentence: NHS stop smoking services offer information and advice and professional support during the first few months after someone stops smoking.
note: Services give information, advice, professional support during first few months

sentence: They provide nicotine replacement therapy, such as patches and gum, and medicines such as varenicline and bupropion.
note: NRT such as patches or gum, and medicines such as varenicline, cytisine and bupropion (Zyban)

sentence: In England people can refer themselves to a local service through the NHS Better Health website, and can also speak to a GP.
note: You can speak to a GP or local Stop Smoking Service; in England self-refer via Better Health

sentence: Availability and arrangements differ between the four UK nations and between areas.
note: Availability and specifics vary by nation and area

sentence: Nicotine replacement therapy comes as patches, gum, lozenges, inhalators and mouth or nasal sprays.
note: NRT also comes as lozenges, inhalators, mouth or nasal sprays

sentence: The NHS describes it as safe, proven to work and able to double the chances of quitting for good.
note: NRTs are safe, proven to work and can double your chances of quitting

sentence: Varenicline works by blocking the effects of nicotine in the brain, which makes smoking less enjoyable and helps with withdrawal symptoms.
note: Varenicline blocks nicotine effects in the brain, making smoking less enjoyable and helping withdrawal

sentence: NHS pages say that a nicotine-free medicine such as varenicline or cytisine can be combined with a nicotine product, and describe the combination as giving the best chance of success.
note: Combining nicotine-free medicine with nicotine product offers best chance of success

sentence: E-cigarettes are not currently available as medicines, so stop smoking services cannot supply them and they cannot be prescribed on the NHS.
note: E-cigarettes are not currently available as medicines so cannot be supplied by stop smoking services or prescribed

sentence: Some local stop smoking services may still offer a free starter pack.
note: Local service may offer a free e-cigarette starter pack

sentence: The NHS sets out a timeline: within about 20 minutes the pulse rate begins to return to normal.
note: NHS timeline: 20 minutes pulse begins to normalise

sentence: By 48 hours carbon monoxide levels in the blood have fallen to those of a non-smoker.
note: 48 hours carbon monoxide reaches non-smoker level

sentence: After one year the risk of a heart attack is about half that of a person who smokes, and after ten years the risk of dying from lung cancer is about half.
note: 1 year heart attack risk roughly halved; 10 years lung cancer death risk about half

sentence: NHS pages also report mental health benefits: once the withdrawal stage has passed, people report less anxiety, depression and stress.
note: After the withdrawal stage, people report less anxiety, depression and stress

sentence: Withdrawal symptoms are temporary, and the NHS lists feeling on edge or anxious and wanting a cigarette among them.
note: Common symptoms include feeling on edge, anxious or craving cigarettes; temporary

sentence: NHS inform, the Scottish NHS site, says cravings improve after the first two to three weeks and that most withdrawal symptoms fade by about two weeks.
note: NHS Inform: cravings improve after first 2 to 3 weeks; most symptoms fade by two weeks

sentence: The NHS says an individual craving lasts only a short time.
note: NHS: cravings last up to 15 minutes

sentence: Walking, chewing sugar-free gum and deep breathing are among the coping ideas it lists.
note: Coping tips include going for a walk, sugar-free gum, deep breathing

sentence: NHS Better Health offers a free personalised quit plan and the NHS Quit Smoking app.
note: NHS offers a free personalised 8-step quit plan and the NHS Quit Smoking app

sentence: In 2024 NHS England announced that the stop smoking medicine cytisine was being rolled out to help people quit.
note: NHS England Nov 2024: NHS rolls out stop-smoking pill (title); search summary: varenicline rolled out late 2024

sentence: The NHS Better Health site says the harm from smoking reaches beyond the lungs, including hearing and vision loss, dementia risk, joint damage and digestive problems.
note: Smoking effects reach beyond lungs: hearing and vision loss, dementia risk, joint damage, digestive problems

sentence: It says smoking damages blood vessels and narrows arteries, and strains the heart by raising blood pressure.
note: Damages blood vessels, narrows arteries, strains heart by raising blood pressure

sentence: The NHS also says smoking increases the risk of developing more than 50 serious health conditions.
note: Smoking increases risk of developing more than 50 serious health conditions

sentence: The relief a cigarette seems to give from stress is short-lived, and smoking can make anxiety and low mood worse over time, according to the NHS.
note: NHS: feeling of a cigarette easing stress is short-lived; can make anxiety and low mood worse over time

sentence: Babies and children living with smoke face a higher risk of chest infections, meningitis and worsening asthma, the NHS says.
note: Babies and children facing higher risk of chest infections, meningitis, worsening asthma
